note: Task #105: performance stability (5 CPU + 7 Vulkan repeated runs) for one representative profile-based mixed-layer config PER MODEL, single prompt (factual_recall_1), ctx=2048, gen_tokens=32.
findings: 360M Vulkan throughput is extremely stable (stdev=0.677 tok/s on a mean of 157.1 tok/s, <0.5% relative spread) -- the tightest of any measured config in this phase.

135M Vulkan throughput shows more spread (stdev=9.885 tok/s on a mean of 278.6 tok/s, ~3.5% relative) than 360M Vulkan, driven by one lower outlier run (258.2 tok/s vs a median of 283.4) -- consistent with this being a shared, memory-constrained dev host with real background load during the run, the same caveat Phase 11C's own CPU numbers carried, not evidence of a genuine KV-mix throughput effect.

CPU throughput for both models is stable within a normal range (135M: 3.7% relative stdev; 360M: 5.5% relative stdev), comparable in magnitude to Phase 11C's own CPU spread (5.5-7.8 tok/s stdev on 50-61 tok/s means for 135M all_q8/all_q5/mixed).

No systematic throughput penalty from per-layer type heterogeneity is evident at either model size on either backend -- consistent with Phase 11B/11C's own finding that mixed Q8/Q5 KV does not measurably slow decode relative to a uniform-type cache.
